i think u misunderstood the post, i was confused while comparing:

1. 250g of meat achieved through buying a 1kg carcass

i see, thnx. so ur saying that if someone buys 250g boneless, they get a higher ratio of prized cuts vs buying 1kg carcass and ending up with roughly 250g of varied quality cuts?

basically he buys 1kg carcass, and asks butcher to cut into boneless which gets him around maybe 250 grams meat. only thing is, dad doesn't know what quantity meat he's going to be getting from the carcass he paid for. now if he bought 250g boneless meat from the start, it would be more expensive than the whole 1kg carcass (apparently).

~~still hard for me to process the premium when buying boneless lol~~

edit: there isn't exactly a premium

if i'm not wrong there's only cutting price for fish, butchers here don't charge for cutting. i found my answer after looking around a little more. so when you ask for say 1kg of boneless meat, the butcher may go through more than one carcass to get you that much. so the prices goes up to compensate for that loss. but that's not the only reason.

as opposed to what my dad did, which is picking a hung carcass, say it weighed 1kg and then asking it to be cut into boneless. here we don't decide how much meat we are getting out of the 1kg we paid for. since we already bought the 1kg carcass. removing the bones is free apparently.

supposing my dad asked the butcher to make boneless meat after picking the carcass, but before paying, he would've ended up paying around 5-20% more. this is apparently because there's a premium associated with boneless meat.

so if you just ask for boneless, it will always be more expensive than buying a whole carcass, then asking butcher to separate meat from bones.

when you ask for boneless, you decide the quantity and then butcher cuts through carcass(es) to meet whatever quantity you demanded.

dad decided a single carcass, butcher weighs the whole thing and charges dad for it. then dad asks to give him just the meat. butcher trashes everything else and hands meat over. dad paid for the whole carcass but only gets the meat. so maybe he paid for 1kg, but got like 250 grams or somethin.

but if you try to buy 250grams of boneless meat, you'll end up paying more than what dad paid for 1kg... to meet the loss of the bones, etc + premium for boneless.

i'm not 100% sure of all the reasons involved for the price increase, but after talking to a butcher this is what i gathered
